q: Circular motion is a specific type of a ____ motion.
e: Circular motion occurs in a plane, making it a specific case of two-dimensional motion.

q: It is a movement of an object along the ____ of a circle (or) rotation along a circular path.
e: In circular motion, the object's path is constrained to the outer boundary or circumference of a circle.

q: We can experience a pulling force (known as the ____) exerted on the ball by the string.
e: When whirling a ball on a string, the string exerts a tension force that keeps the ball in circular motion.

q: Other examples of the circular motion are a satellite orbiting the earth, motion of a wheel, turning of a car around ____ respectively.
e: A car turning follows a curved path, which is a practical example of circular motion in everyday life.

q: If an object (rigid body) rotates about an axis, each particle consisting of the object moves in a ____ motion.
e: In a rotating rigid body, every individual particle traces out a circular path around the axis of rotation.

q: Although an object moves in a circle at a constant speed, its ____ is not constant.
e: Velocity is a vector quantity, so even if the speed is constant, the continuously changing direction means the velocity is not constant.

q: The direction of the velocity is ____ to the path.
e: At any given point in circular motion, the velocity vector points tangent to the circular path.

q: Velocity is constantly changing because the ____ of the velocity is changing continuously.
e: The continuous change in the direction of motion is what causes the velocity to change, resulting in acceleration.

q: The velocity in circular motion is also called the ____ velocity.
e: Because it is always directed tangent to the circular path, the linear velocity in circular motion is referred to as tangential velocity.

q: In this time interval, it has rotated through an angle $\theta$ with respect to the reference line and through a distance s measured along the circumference of the circle, called an ____ length.
e: The distance traveled along the curved path of the circle is known as the arc length.

q: Change of the angular position is called the angular ____.
e: Angular displacement measures the angle through which an object has rotated from its initial reference position.

q: The angular displacement is the ratio of the arc length to ____.
e: By definition, angular displacement in radians is the arc length divided by the radius of the circle.

q: The magnitude of angular displacement ($\theta$), measured in radian (rad), is given by $\theta = $ ____.
e: This formula defines the radian measure of an angle as the ratio of the subtended arc length to the radius.

q: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the ____ of the circle.
e: This is the fundamental geometric definition of one radian.

q: If $s = r$, $\theta = $ ____.
e: When the arc length equals the radius, the angular displacement is exactly one radian.
One full revolution around a circle corresponds to an angle of $2\pi$ radians.

q: Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to ____ taken.
e: Average angular velocity measures how much angular displacement occurs per unit of time.

q: Average angular velocity is given by $\omega_{avg} = \frac{\theta_2 - \theta_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: This is the standard formula for calculating average angular velocity over a finite time interval.

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular velocity can be written as $\omega = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \theta}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous angular velocity is the first derivative of angular displacement with respect to time.

q: Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: This is the formal definition of instantaneous angular velocity.

q: At constant angular velocity, $\omega = $ ____.
e: When angular velocity is constant, it can be simply calculated as the total angular displacement divided by the total time.

q: Angular velocity is measured in radian per second (rad s$^{-1}$), revolution per second (rps) and revolution per ____ (rpm or rev min$^{-1}$).
e: Revolutions per minute (rpm) is a common practical unit for measuring angular velocity, especially in machinery.

q: The average angular acceleration is the ratio of change of angular velocity to ____ taken.
e: Average angular acceleration measures the rate at which angular velocity changes over a given time period.

q: The average angular acceleration is given by $\alpha_{avg} = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: This formula calculates the average rate of change of angular velocity.

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular acceleration can be defined as $\alpha = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \omega}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the first derivative of angular velocity with respect to time.

q: The instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: This is the formal definition of instantaneous angular acceleration.

q: When a body is moving with a constant angular acceleration, $\alpha = $ ____.
e: For constant angular acceleration, it is calculated as the change in angular velocity divided by the time taken.

q: Angular acceleration is measured in radian per second squared (rad s$^{-2}$) and revolution per ____ squared (rev s$^{-2}$).
e: The standard SI unit for angular acceleration is radians per second squared.

q: The magnitude of the angular velocity (angular speed) is related to that of the ____ velocity (tangential speed) as follows.
e: There is a direct proportional relationship between angular speed and tangential speed for a given radius.

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation between tangential speed and angular speed is $v = $ ____.
e: Tangential velocity is the product of the radius of the circular path and the angular velocity.

q: The relation between the angular acceleration $\alpha$ and the tangential acceleration $a_t$ is $a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = $ ____.
e: Tangential acceleration is the time derivative of tangential velocity.

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation simplifies to $a_t = $ ____.
e: Tangential acceleration is the product of the radius and the angular acceleration.

q: In Eq.(1.17), the direction of linear acceleration $a_t$ is ____ to the path.
e: Tangential acceleration acts along the tangent to the circular path, changing the speed of the object.

q: It is called the ____ acceleration.
e: This component of acceleration is specifically named for its direction tangent to the circular path.
